**1.224.17**  Vaiśaṃpāyana said: After the fire had passed beyond that region, Jaritā, full of longing for her little ones, quickly rushed toward her children.

**1.224.18**  She found all of them safe and sound in the forest, freed from Jātavedas, and she saw her sons weeping piteously.

**1.224.19**  Finding their sight almost too wonderful to believe, she went to each of her crying sons one by one, again and again.

**1.224.20**  Then Mandapāla also came quickly, O Bhārata. But all his sons did not greet him with joy.

**1.224.21**  Though he lamented to each of them one by one and to Jaritā again and again, they did not speak a single word to that sage — neither kind nor harsh.

**1.224.22**  Mandapāla said: Which is your eldest son? Which comes after him? Which son is the middle one? And which is your youngest?

**1.224.23**  Why do you not respond to me as I speak in distress? I made a pact with the fire-eater; and yet I find no peace here.

**1.224.24**  Jaritā said: What business do you have with the eldest son? Or with the one who comes after him? What business do you have with the middle one, or with the youngest, you wretched man?

**1.224.25**  You who abandoned me utterly and went away before — go back to that young Lapitā with her lovely smile.

**1.224.26**  Mandapāla said: For women there is nothing at all besides another man. Rivalry between co-wives is inescapable — it must be so in the world.

**1.224.27**  Even the virtuous and beautiful Arundhatī, renowned throughout all the worlds, suspected Vasiṣṭha, the greatest of sages.

**1.224.28**  She despised that utterly pure-hearted sage, ever devoted to her welfare and benefit, that hero dwelling among the seven sages.

**1.224.29**  Through that suspicion, her radiance became like smoky red; she can be barely seen, dim and without her former beauty — she is perceived now only as a pale mark.

**1.224.30**  I came here for the sake of offspring, and so you too are now forsaking the beloved and acting in the same way.

**1.224.31**  A man should never place total trust in a wife, for a wife who is a true mother of sons does not think of a husband's duty.

**1.224.32**  Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then all his sons attended upon him properly, and he began to comfort his children, O king.

**1.225.1**  Mandapāla said: For the sake of protecting you I petitioned the fire, and the fire promised accordingly — "So be it" — even before this.

**1.225.2**  Knowing the word of the fire, your mother's knowledge of dharma, and your own supreme valor, I did not come here sooner.

**1.225.3**  You should not grieve over death, my dear children. Even the fire knows the sages and the sacred knowledge of Brahman; and you too understand this.

**1.225.4**  Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having thus comforted his sons and taking his wife with him, O Bhārata, Mandapāla departed from that place to another region.

**1.225.5**  The divine sharp-rayed fire also burned the blazing Khāṇḍava forest together with the two Kṛṣṇas, generating fearlessness for the world.

**1.225.6**  Drinking streams of fat and marrow flowing there, the purifying fire attained supreme satisfaction and revealed himself to Arjuna.

**1.225.7**  Then the lord of the gods, surrounded by the hosts of Maruts, descended from the sky and spoke these words to Pārtha and to Mādhava.

**1.225.8**  Indra said: You two have accomplished a feat difficult even for the immortals. Choose your boons — I am pleased; choose even those that are rare and beyond human reach.

**1.225.9**  Pārtha then chose from Śakra to receive all weapons in full; and Śakra set a proper time for granting them to him.

**1.225.10**  Indra said: When the divine Mahādeva shall be graciously disposed toward you, then I will grant you all the weapons of the Pāṇḍavas.

**1.225.11**  I myself will know that moment, O delight of the Kurus; and through great austerity I too shall grant those weapons to you.

**1.225.12**  All the weapons of Agni, all those of Vāyu as well, and all those that are mine — all of these you shall receive, O Dhanañjaya.

**1.225.13**  Vāsudeva also obtained eternal friendship with Pārtha; and the lord of gods, greatly pleased, granted him that boon at that time.

**1.225.14**  Having joyfully granted the boon to both of them, the lord of the Maruts, together with the gods, took leave of the fire and returned to the triple heaven.

**1.225.15**  The fire too, having burned that forest along with its animals and birds, rested for five days and one more, fully satisfied.

**1.225.16**  Having devoured the flesh and drunk the fat and blood, filled with supreme delight, he spoke to those two, O lord of the people.

**1.225.17**  Fire said: By the two of you, foremost among men, I have been satisfied to my full contentment. I grant you leave, O heroes; go wherever you desire.

**1.225.18**  Thus were those two — Arjuna and Vāsudeva — granted leave by the great-souled fire, as was the demon Maya.

**1.225.19**  Then all three of them, O bull of the Bhāratas, having circumambulated the fire, sat down together on the pleasant bank of the river.
